title: Epic: a daily practice rhythm
body: ## Problem
The trainer works when you open it, but nothing brings you back. The owner's own account shows
the pattern: 8 positions due on the overview, done on Monday, then nothing until the weekend. The
only streak in the app is per item (`streak` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`), which the
player never sees. There is no daily goal and no reminder.
## Who it's for
A club player (800 to 1500 rapid) who wants to improve, plays most days, and forgets to practise.
## Goals
- One small daily goal: finish today's session (at most `SESSION_SIZE` positions).
- A streak that forgives one missed day a week, shown where the session is offered.
- An opt-in email in the morning with today's count, off by default.
## Non-goals
- Points, badges, leaderboards or any reward for volume. The research says no points for volume.
- Push notifications or a mobile app.
- Changing the spacing schedule (1, 3, 7, 21, 60 days) or the daily cap.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, "Streaks and daily goal": a small daily goal
with a streak that tolerates a missed day (Lally et al., habit formation), and Duolingo's result
that separating the daily goal from the streak raised day-14 retention. Ranked 2nd in the
end-user review of 2026-11-23.
## Proposed design
- Data: none new for the streak. It is computed from `drill_attempts.at`, read as calendar
days in the player's time zone (`dayOf` in `model.ts`, the zone from `requestTimeZone()`).
- Rule: a day counts when the player answered at least one position that day. The streak is
the run of counted days ending today or yesterday, where one uncounted day per ISO week is a rest
day. Example: Mon, Tue, (Wed off), Thu, Fri is a 4-day streak; missing Thu as well ends it.
- UX: the practise card on the overview (`_overview/practise-card.tsx`) and the trainer page
show "4-day streak" from 2 days up, and nothing below that. No flame, no confetti: one line in
the card's existing type, per `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`.
- Email: a per-user setting (`practice_email`, off by default) and a send time in the player's
morning. The email says how many positions are due and links to `/app/train`, nothing else.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A pure `streakOf(days, today)` in `model.ts`, with the rest-day rule, covered by unit tests
across a week boundary and a DST change.
- [ ] The practise card and the trainer show the streak from 2 days, in day and night, 390 px and
1440 px, with screenshots in the PR.
- [ ] The daily email is opt-in, has a one-click unsubscribe, and is never sent on a day with
nothing due.
- [ ] A short ADR records the streak rule and the email schedule.
## Test plan
- Unit: `streakOf`, and the email's "who gets one today" query.
- e2e: the card's streak line after attempts on two days (seeded, like `train.spec.ts`).
- Visual: the practise card's baselines at 390 and 1440, day and night.
## ADR
Yes, the next free number: the streak rule and the email (it is the first mail that is not a
sign-in link).
## Risks and open questions
- The email needs a scheduler. The Rust worker has one (`backend/crates/scheduler`), but mail is
sent from the web app today (`apps/web/src/server/mail.ts`). Which side sends it?
- Should a session finished after midnight count for the day before?
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`dayOf`, `SESSION_SIZE`, `DAILY_CAP`, `practiseToday`)
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-card.tsx` and `practise-view.ts`
- ADR 0090 (the trainer), ADR 0092 (the focused overview)

title: Show a practice streak that forgives one rest day a week
parent: Epic: a daily practice rhythm
body: ## Problem
A player who practised five days running sees nothing for it. The practise card on the overview
says "Practise today: 8 positions due" whether this is their first day or their fortieth.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `streakOf(days: string[], today: string): number` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`.
`days` are the distinct calendar days with an attempt, in the player's zone (`dayOf`). One
uncounted day per ISO week is a rest day; a second one ends the streak.
- [ ] Unit tests: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri is 4; Mon, Thu is 0 on Fri; a streak across a Sunday to Monday
boundary; a DST change in Europe/London; today not practised yet still shows yesterday's
streak.
- [ ] The days come from one query on `drill_attempts` (distinct days, last 60), not one per day.
- [ ] The card in `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-card.tsx` shows "4-day streak"
from 2 days up, and nothing below 2. Tokens only (`pnpm design:check` passes).
- [ ] Screenshots at 390 px and 1440 px, day and night, in the PR.
## Pointers
- The parent epic has the full spec and the research link.
- `apps/web/test/train/model.test.ts` already tests `dayOf` across DST: copy that style.
- `packages/ui/DESIGN.md` before touching the card.

title: Opt-in morning email with today's practice positions
parent: Epic: a daily practice rhythm
body: ## Problem
Players forget to practise on the days they do not open the app. A reminder they asked for is
the cheapest way back, and today Rematch sends no mail except the sign-in link.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A setting on the account page: "Email me in the morning when positions are due", off by
default, stored per user (a new migration in `db/migrations/`).
- [ ] One email per day at most, at about 08:00 in the zone the player last used, only when
something is due, with the count and one link to `/app/train`.
- [ ] Every email has a one-click unsubscribe link that works signed out.
- [ ] No email address or name in any outbound request other than the mail itself (ADR 0043).
- [ ] Tests: who gets an email today (due, opted in, not already sent), the unsubscribe token, and
an e2e that reads the mail from Mailpit.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/mail.ts` sends the sign-in mail today.
- `backend/crates/scheduler` runs the worker's periodic jobs.
- ADR 0043 (no email in outbound requests). Decide in the PR which side sends the mail, and record
it in the epic's ADR.

title: Epic: answer "Is it working?" sooner
body: ## Problem
"Is it working?" on `/app/train` waits for 30 chances on each side of the first drill and for the
80% intervals to separate (`MIN_CHANCES` and `verdictOf` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`).
That is the right bar, but a player sees "Too early to tell: 9 chances in games since your first
drill, and 30 are needed" for weeks, with no idea whether that means three games or thirty. The
owner's account, with about 22% of positions held back, needs weeks of rapid games to reach it.
Invisible progress is where people stop practising.
## Who it's for
Every trainer user in their first month, which is everyone until the first verdict.
## Goals
- Say how far away the verdict is, in games, not chances.
- Show the numbers that are already trustworthy: positions answered, and first-try accuracy on
repeats, with n and an 80% interval like every other rate.
## Non-goals
- Lowering `MIN_CHANCES` or calling a change on overlapping intervals. The honesty rules stay.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 4, "How to measure that it works", and the
end-user review of 2026-11-23 (ranked 3rd): motivation depends on seeing progress.
## Proposed design
- ETA: chances per game from the player's recent games in the scope (the same counting the
"after" side uses), then `ceil((30 - chances) / rate)`. Shown as "about 14 more rapid games at
your recent pace". With fewer than 5 recent games, no estimate.
- Training stats: positions answered, and first-try accuracy by repetition (1st, 2nd, 3rd
showing), each with n and the 80% interval from the existing rate helpers.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The too-early lines in `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts` carry the ETA in games
when there is a pace to estimate from, and keep today's wording when there is not.
- [ ] A training-stats block on `/app/train` with n and an 80% range on every rate, a dash for no
data, never a fake 0%.
- [ ] Unit tests for the ETA (no games, slow pace, already enough) and for the stats.
## Test plan
- Unit: `apps/web/test/train/copy.test.ts` and `model.test.ts`.
- e2e: extend the "trainer states" test in `apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts` with the ETA line.
## ADR
An amendment to ADR 0090 for the ETA formula is enough.
## Risks and open questions
- The pace changes: a player who stops playing gets an estimate that never arrives. Show the date
of the last game the pace came from?
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`MIN_CHANCES`, `verdictOf`, the before and after rates)
- `apps/web/src/server/train/store.ts` (where the rates are loaded)

title: Say how many more games "Is it working?" needs
parent: Epic: answer "Is it working?" sooner
body: ## Problem
"Too early to tell: 9 chances in games since your first drill, and 30 are needed." A player has
no idea how many games that is. At 2 chances a game it is about 11 rapid games; at 0.3 it is
months.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A pure function in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` that returns the games still needed
from the chances so far, `MIN_CHANCES`, and the chances per game over the scope's recent
games; `null` with fewer than 5 recent games or a pace of 0.
- [ ] `copy.ts` adds "about 11 more rapid games at your recent pace" to the too-early lines when
the estimate is not null; the wording stays as it is otherwise.
- [ ] Unit tests: no recent games, a pace of 0, already at 30, a fractional result rounded up.
- [ ] The "trainer states" e2e in `apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts` checks the new line.
## Pointers
- `MIN_CHANCES` and `verdictOf` in `model.ts`; the too-early copy is in
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts` (lines starting "Too early to tell").
- The parent epic has the full spec.

title: Show first-try accuracy on repeated positions
parent: Epic: answer "Is it working?" sooner
body: ## Problem
The one number that moves in the first week is whether you get a position right the second and
third time you see it. Rematch stores every attempt in `drill_attempts` and shows none of this.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For the scope: positions answered, and first-try accuracy at the 1st, 2nd and 3rd showing of
an item, each with n and the 80% interval (the helpers `copy.ts` already uses for rates).
- [ ] A dash, not 0%, when a showing has no attempts.
- [ ] One aggregate query, grouped in SQL, not a row per attempt.
- [ ] Unit tests for the grouping (a same-day second attempt is not a new showing; it is not
recorded at all, see the store tests).
- [ ] Shown on `/app/train` under "Is it working?", with screenshots at 390 and 1440 px.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/store.ts` (`attemptsByItem` is the closest existing query)
- `apps/web/test/train/store.test.ts`
- The parent epic.

title: Epic: drills for every weekly focus
body: ## Problem
The weekly focus can be any ranked weakness, but the trainer only has positions for five sources:
`W4.missed`, `W3.shallow`, `W3.deep`, `W7.traps` and `blunder` (`SOURCES` in
`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`). Pick "Getting short of time" (W9a) or "Opening
preparation" (W7.prep) as your focus and the practise card quietly serves every source instead
(`practiseToday` falls back when the focus source has no items). The player is told to work on
their clock and handed a mate-in-two.
The trap positions that are drilled are drilled as one move: the owner's account has 71 `W7.traps`
items, each the single move after the trap, never the line that led into it.
## Who it's for
Players whose top weakness is in the opening or on the clock, which at 800 to 1200 rapid is common.
## Goals
- Every focus either has a drill or says plainly that it has none yet.
- An opening-trap trainer that replays the line from move 1.
- A clock-budget check for the time weaknesses (W9a to W9d), as feedback after each game.
## Non-goals
- Drills for W12 (tilt) or W10 (quiet positions) in this epic.
- A general opening repertoire trainer. Only the lines where the player actually fell for a trap.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, features 4 (opening-trap trainer) and 6
(clock discipline). The clock feature has the weakest drill evidence there, so it is feedback, not
a drill. Finding R2-3 of the 2026-11-23 holistic review.
## Proposed design
- Honest fallback first: the practise card names the focus and says it has no drills yet.
- Trap lines: a new item kind, a line from move 1 to the trap position as the player's colour.
The opponent's moves come from the player's own game; the player's move passes when it is the
game's move or within 30 centipawns of the engine's best. The final question is the existing
single-move drill.
- Clock budget: per time class, a budget per phase taken from the research (at most 15% of
the clock by move 10, at least 20% left at move 30), checked after each game from the stored
clocks, with the share of games that reach low-time trouble as the goal number.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The fallback is visible (sub-issue).
- [ ] A trap-line session on `/app/train?source=W7.traps` that replays the line, with tests.
- [ ] A clock-budget line in the game review and a weekly rate on the focus card for W9 focuses.
- [ ] An ADR for the trap-line item kind and one for the clock budget.
## Test plan
- Unit: line grading, the budget check per phase.
- e2e: a trap-line session from the seeded fixtures; the W9 focus card.
- Visual: the trainer's line mode and the budget line, 390 and 1440, day and night.
## ADR
Yes, two: the trap-line item kind (it changes `drill_items`) and the clock budget.
## Risks and open questions
- Trap lines from the player's own game can contain the opponent's mistakes. Is that the line to
learn, or should the opponent's replies come from the opening explorer (ADR 0012)?
- Stored clocks are missing for some chess.com games; the budget must say "no clock data".
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`SOURCES`, `practiseToday`), `store.ts`
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-view.ts`
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` (W7, W9)
- ADR 0090 (trainer), ADR 0091 (weekly focus), ADR 0012 (opening explorer)

title: Say so when the weekly focus has no drills
parent: Epic: drills for every weekly focus
body: ## Problem
Set "Getting short of time" as your weekly focus and the overview says "Practise today: 8
positions due", then serves missed mates and blunders. Nothing tells you those positions are not
about your focus. The fallback is deliberate (`practiseToday` in
`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`); hiding it is not.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the focus is set and its weakness is not one of `SOURCES`, the practise card's detail
line says so, for example: "Getting short of time has no drills yet, so today's positions
come from all your missed moments."
- [ ] The weakness name comes from the glossary (`apps/web/src/server/profile/glossary.ts`), not
a hard-coded string.
- [ ] A unit test in `apps/web/test/train/practise.test.ts` next to "keeps the focus source when
it has items, and falls back to every source when not".
- [ ] No change when the focus has drills, or when there is no focus.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-view.ts` builds the card's words.
- About 2 hours for someone new to the code. Ask in the issue if the focus is not reaching
`practiseView`; it may need one more argument.

title: Opening-trap line trainer: replay the line from move 1
parent: Epic: drills for every weekly focus
body: ## Problem
You fell for the Fried Liver three times. The trainer shows you the position after 6.Nxf7 and asks
for one move. It never makes you play the five moves that walked into it, which is the part you
would repeat in your next game.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A trap-line item kind for `W7.traps` positions: the moves from the start to the trap, the
player's colour, and the final question (the existing single-move drill).
- [ ] The player plays their side's moves; each passes when it is the move from their game or
within 30 centipawns of the engine's best (the research's grading rule).
- [ ] A wrong move shows the right one and the line continues; the item's schedule follows the
final answer only.
- [ ] Held-out items stay held out (the "Is it working?" control group must not leak).
- [ ] Unit tests for line grading, an e2e for one full line, screenshots of the line mode.
## Pointers
- [Research, feature 4](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md).
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (sources, grading), `store.ts` (items)
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` (`W7.traps`)
- Needs the epic's ADR before code; comment on the epic first.

title: Clock budget for time-trouble focuses, checked after each game
parent: Epic: drills for every weekly focus
body: ## Problem
A player whose top weakness is "Getting short of time" (W9a) or "Blunders on a low clock" (W9b)
gets a weekly focus with nothing to do about it. The research says clock discipline works as
feedback, not as a drill: a budget per phase, and a check after each game.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A budget per time class: at most 15% of the clock used by move 10, at least 20% left at
move 30 (configurable constants, cited to the research in the code).
- [ ] After each analysed game: within budget or not, per phase, from the stored clocks; "no clock
data" when clocks are missing, never a guess.
- [ ] The focus card for a W9 focus shows the share of this week's games that reached low-time
trouble, with n.
- [ ] Unit tests for the budget check, including increments and missing clocks.
## Pointers
- [Research, feature 6](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md).
- W9a to W9d in `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` and their names in
`apps/web/src/server/profile/glossary.ts`.
- ADR 0091 (weekly focus).

title: Epic: conversion play-outs against an opponent at your level
body: ## Problem
"Not winning won games" (W5) is a real weakness at club level: the owner's profile shows 7 of 20
won positions not converted as Black. The trainer can only ask for one move, but conversion is a
skill of many moves: trading down, stopping counterplay, not rushing. There is no way to practise
it in Rematch today.
## Who it's for
Players with W5 among their top weaknesses, and anyone whose trajectory shows the score slipping
while accuracy holds.
## Goals
- Play your own won positions on, against an opponent at your opponent's level, and get graded.
- Show where the advantage collapsed when you fail.
## Non-goals
- Playing full games against an engine. A play-out starts from your position and ends early.
- Running without Maia. Stockfish's `UCI_LimitStrength` floor is 1320 Elo, stronger than many of
our players' opponents, so a weaker Stockfish would grade the wrong skill. Without Maia the
feature is hidden, and the page says why.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, feature 3: the player's own +3 positions
that ended in a draw or loss, played on against Maia at the opponent's rating. Ranked 5th in the
end-user review of 2026-11-23.
## Proposed design
- Positions: the W5 episodes the detector already finds (`w5` in
`backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs`): the first position of a winning
episode the player did not win.
- Opponent: the Maia service (`services/maia`, `POST /v1/predict` with `eloSelf` and
`eloOppo`), playing the most likely move at the opponent's rating from the game.
- Grading: pass when the player wins, reaches a tablebase win (5 pieces or fewer, Syzygy), or
keeps the evaluation in the win band for 20 moves without a drop of 2 pawns or more.
- Schedule: 3, 10 and 30 days, one or two play-outs a session.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Play-out positions are made by the worker from W5 episodes (sub-issue).
- [ ] A play-out session in the trainer against Maia (sub-issue).
- [ ] With Maia off, no play-out appears anywhere, and the trainer says Maia is needed.
- [ ] An ADR for the play-out item, its grading and its schedule.
## Test plan
- Rust: episode-to-position extraction, with fixtures.
- Web: grading as a pure function; an e2e against a fake Maia that plays fixed moves.
## ADR
Yes, the next free number.
## Risks and open questions
- Maia needs a GPU-free host with enough memory; check the self-host profile.
- Engine evaluation every move costs worker time. Evaluate only every few moves?
## Pointers
- `services/maia`, `docker-compose.maia.yml`, ADR-R2-13 (Maia licence and difficulty), ADR 0010
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` (`w5`, episodes)
- ADR-R2-12 (Syzygy), ADR 0090 (trainer)

title: Make play-out positions from unconverted winning episodes
parent: Epic: conversion play-outs against an opponent at your level
body: ## Problem
The W5 detector finds every winning episode a player did not convert, but only counts it. The
positions are thrown away, so there is nothing to play out.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For each failed W5 episode, the worker stores the episode's first position (FEN), the
player's colour, the opponent's rating at the time, and the ply where the advantage dropped.
- [ ] Stored once per episode (idempotent across re-analysis), in a new table from a migration in
`db/migrations/`, regenerated into Drizzle with `sh scripts/db/generate-drizzle-schema.sh`.
- [ ] Integration tests with `#[sqlx::test(migrator = "db::MIGRATOR")]` on fixture games: a won
game makes none, a drawn won position makes one, re-analysis makes no duplicate.
## Pointers
- `w5` and `episodes` in `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs`
- The parent epic's spec; its ADR decides the table before code.

title: Play out a won position against Maia in the trainer
parent: Epic: conversion play-outs against an opponent at your level
body: ## Problem
Once play-out positions exist, the player needs a board to play them on: their moves against
Maia's at the opponent's rating, until the position is won, held for 20 moves, or lost.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A play-out mode on `/app/train` that sends each position to the Maia service and plays its
most likely move at the stored opponent rating.
- [ ] Grading as a pure, tested function: a win, a Syzygy win, or 20 moves in the win band without
a 2-pawn drop pass; anything else fails and marks the move where the band was lost.
- [ ] With Maia off, the mode does not appear.
- [ ] An e2e against a fake Maia with fixed replies; screenshots at 390 and 1440 px.
## Pointers
- `services/maia/app/main.py` (the `/v1/predict` contract)
- The `chess-ui` skill and `packages/ui/DESIGN.md` before the board work.
- The parent epic.

title: Epic: a pipeline benchmark scorecard, tiers 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
We say the worker is fast, and nobody can check it. There are measurements, but each in its own
place: `lichess-db bench` for the reference pipeline
(`docs/research/r2-lichess-db-benchmark.md`), per-stage timings in the database (ADR 0036),
`cli eta` for one account. A change that halves throughput would pass CI, and a self-hoster has
no way to compare their machine with ours.
## Who it's for
Contributors changing the analysis path, and self-hosters sizing a machine.
## Goals
One JSON scorecard, made by one command, with four tiers:
1. **Engine:** positions a second for one Stockfish thread at the pinned protocol (ADR 0007).
2. **One account:** a fixed set of fixture games imported, analysed and profiled end to end;
games an hour and the per-stage split (ADR 0036).
3. **Reference build:** the `lichess-db` pipeline on the synthetic input, games a second.
4. **Coach:** report wall time, tokens in and out, and statements the validator dropped per
report (ADR 0093), on a fixed coaching input. Live tokens cost money, so tier 4 is run by a
maintainer, never in CI.
## Non-goals
- A benchmark that gates CI. Shared runners are too noisy; the scorecard is a trend.
## Evidence
The research notes already record tier-3 numbers by hand; making them repeatable is the point.
## Proposed design
- `cli bench --tiers 1,2,3 --json` writes one file with the machine (CPU, cores, memory), the
commit, the Stockfish version and each tier's numbers.
- The monthly maintenance sweep adds a row from the maintainer's machine; the site shows the trend.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tiers 1 to 4 each have a sub-issue done.
- [ ] One JSON schema for every tier, checked by a test.
- [ ] The scorecard page on the site reads the committed results.
## Test plan
- Rust: the JSON schema and the tier runners on tiny inputs.
- Site: the scorecard page renders from a fixture file.
## ADR
Yes: what each tier measures and where the results live.
## Risks and open questions
- The fixture games for tier 2 must be ours to publish: generated or CC0 games from the Lichess
database, never a real chess.com player's history.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/lichess-db` (`bench`), `backend/crates/cli` (`eta`, `queue-lag`)
- `docs/research/r2-lichess-db-benchmark.md`
- ADR 0007, ADR 0036, ADR 0093, ADR-R2-16 (tiered analysis scheduler)

title: Benchmark tiers 1 and 2: one engine thread and one account end to end
parent: Epic: a pipeline benchmark scorecard, tiers 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
There is no repeatable number for how fast one Stockfish thread analyses positions under our
protocol, or how long one account's games take from import to profile.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cli bench --tiers 1,2 --json` in `backend/crates/cli`.
- [ ] Tier 1: positions a second for one thread, at the protocol pinned in ADR 0007, on a fixed set
of FENs checked into the crate's test data.
- [ ] Tier 2: a fixed set of CC0 or generated fixture games through import, analysis and profile,
with games an hour and the per-stage split that ADR 0036 records.
- [ ] The JSON includes the commit, CPU model, core count, memory and Stockfish version.
- [ ] A test that runs both tiers on tiny inputs and validates the JSON shape.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/lichess-db` already has a `bench` command; reuse its timing code.
- ADR 0007, ADR 0036. The parent epic has the schema discussion.

title: Benchmark tiers 3 and 4: the reference build and the coach report
parent: Epic: a pipeline benchmark scorecard, tiers 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
`lichess-db bench` prints its numbers in its own format, and nobody measures what a coach report
costs. Report quality is measurable already (statements dropped by the validator, ADR 0093), but
only by reading the database.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tier 3: `lichess-db bench` writes the scorecard's JSON shape (`--json`).
- [ ] Tier 4: a maintainer-only command that builds one report from a fixed coaching input and
records wall time, input and output tokens, and dropped statements by reason.
- [ ] Tier 4 refuses to run in CI (`CI` set) and never runs without an explicit flag: it spends
real tokens.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/lichess-db`, `backend/crates/ai`
- `docs/research/r2-lichess-db-benchmark.md`, ADR 0093 (validator false drops), ADR 0062

title: Scorecard page on the site with the trend across releases
parent: Epic: a pipeline benchmark scorecard, tiers 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
Benchmark results that live in a JSON file nobody opens do not stop regressions. The public site
is where self-hosters and contributors look.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/benchmarks/*.json` (one file per run) rendered at `/docs/benchmarks/` by the site's
build, like the decision log (`site/scripts/sync-content.mjs`).
- [ ] One table per tier with the machine, the commit and the number; a sparkline is optional.
- [ ] A site test renders the page from a fixture file; `pnpm --filter @ci/site links` passes.
## Pointers
- `site/scripts/sync-content.mjs` and `site/test/content-lib.test.ts`
- The parent epic's JSON schema.

title: A low-memory profile: the whole stack in 3 GB
body: ## Problem
The full compose stack uses about 4 to 5 GB of memory while it analyses. On an 8 GB laptop with a
browser open, Docker runs out and the worker is killed mid-game. Most self-hosters analyse one
account and do not need the throughput.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An overlay `docker-compose.small.yml`: one Stockfish thread, worker concurrency 1, smaller
Postgres buffers, no Maia.
- [ ] Measured with `docker stats` while analysing 100 games: peak under 3 GB, numbers in the PR.
- [ ] The analysis results are the same as the default profile's (same protocol, only slower).
- [ ] Documented in the self-hosting docs with the measured numbers.
## Pointers
- `docker-compose.yml` and the existing overlays (`docker-compose.maia.yml`, `*.ports.yml`)
- ADR 0007 (the analysis protocol must not change), ADR 0045 (worker runtime)

title: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
Rematch reads chess.com games only. Lichess players, and anyone with over-the-board games in a
PGN file, cannot use it. The Lichess code exists: the importer
(`backend/crates/platforms/src/lichess.rs`), OAuth linking (ADR-WEB-4,
`apps/web/src/server/accounts/lichess-link.ts`) and the `LICHESS_ENABLED` flag
(`apps/web/src/env.ts`, off by default since ADR-FIX-N-1). It was parked by ADR 0040 to finish
chess.com first, and nobody has walked a Lichess account through every page since.
## Who it's for
Lichess players, and club players who record tournament games.
## Goals
- With `LICHESS_ENABLED=1`, a Lichess account works on every page a chess.com account does.
- A PGN file can be imported as its own source, for one user only.
## Non-goals
- Turning Lichess on by default in this epic: that is a maintainer decision after it is proven.
- Importing other people's games from a PGN (a club's whole tournament).
## Evidence
Lichess has the larger share of free players, and OTB games are where club players most want
feedback. ADR 0040 says re-enabling Lichess is "a scheduling change, not a rewrite"; this epic
checks that claim.
## Proposed design
- Lichess: an audit page by page with the e2e fakes, fixing what breaks. Ratings are Lichess's
own, so no band mapping; the chess.com peer benchmark (ADR 0080) does not apply and must say so.
- PGN: a `pgn` platform whose games belong to one user, imported by `cli import-pgn` first and an
upload form later.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every app page has an e2e path with a Lichess account against the fakes (sub-issue).
- [ ] PGN import from the CLI, with the privacy rule decided in an ADR (sub-issue).
## Test plan
- e2e with the Lichess fake (`docker-compose.e2e.yml`, tag `@fakes`).
- Rust fixture tests for PGN parsing (clocks, missing headers, variants refused).
## ADR
Yes for PGN (a new platform, and other players' names in OTB headers). An amendment to ADR 0040
when Lichess is proven.
## Risks and open questions
- OTB games have no clocks, so W9 weaknesses are unknown for them and must not count as zero.
## Pointers
- ADR 0040, ADR-FIX-N-1, ADR-WEB-4, ADR 0080
- `backend/crates/platforms/src/lichess.rs`, `apps/web/src/server/accounts/lichess-link.ts`

title: Walk a Lichess account through every page with LICHESS_ENABLED=1
parent: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
The Lichess importer, linking and sign-in exist but have been off since ADR 0040. Nobody knows
which pages still assume chess.com: the peer benchmark is chess.com only (ADR 0080), and copy
like "your chess.com games" is common.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An e2e spec, tagged `@fakes`, that links a Lichess account against the fake and visits the
overview, games, a game review, weaknesses, progress, the trainer and the coach.
- [ ] Every page names the right platform, and the peer benchmark says it is chess.com only
instead of showing a chess.com comparison.
- [ ] A list in the PR of what was broken and how it was fixed.
- [ ] No real Lichess account is linked in any test or fixture.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e/accounts.spec.ts` (the existing Lichess linking specs), `docker-compose.e2e.yml`
- `apps/web/src/env.ts` (`LICHESS_ENABLED`), ADR-FIX-N-1, ADR 0040

title: Import over-the-board games from a PGN file
parent: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
Club players want feedback on their tournament games most of all, and those games live in PGN
files, not on chess.com.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cli import-pgn --user <id> --file games.pgn --name <your name in the PGN>` imports the games
where the named player played, as a `pgn` source owned by that user only.
- [ ] Variants, games without moves and duplicates (same moves, date and players) are refused or
skipped, and the CLI says how many and why.
- [ ] Games without clocks leave the time weaknesses unknown, never zero.
- [ ] An ADR covers the new platform and the opponent names in PGN headers (privacy, ADR 0018).
- [ ] Rust tests with fixture PGNs.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/platforms` (the chess.com and Lichess importers to copy), `backend/crates/cli`
- ADR 0018 (privacy defaults), ADR 0025 (tiered import)

title: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
Every word in the app is English, written inline in components and `copy.ts` files, and numbers
and dates are formatted for `en-GB` by hand in places (`practise-view.ts` has its own list of
month names). Chess is played everywhere; a Spanish or German club player cannot use Rematch.
## Who it's for
Players who do not read English comfortably, and contributors who want to translate.
## Goals
- A message catalogue and a locale per user, starting with the overview and the trainer.
- Numbers and dates from `Intl` with the user's locale everywhere.
## Non-goals
- Translating the AI coach's reports in this epic (the validator checks English text).
- Translating the docs site.
## Evidence
Requests from the beta will decide the first language; the scaffolding is the same for any.
## Proposed design
- Choose a library that works with the App Router's server components (an ADR compares two).
- One catalogue per locale under `apps/web/messages/`, keys by page.
- `Stat` already takes a `locale` (`packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`); pass the user's.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An ADR picking the library.
- [ ] No hand-written month or number formatting left (sub-issue).
- [ ] The overview and the trainer read every string from the catalogue, with English as the only
complete locale and a test that fails on a missing key.
## Test plan
- Unit: the missing-key test.
- e2e and visual: the overview in English unchanged (the baselines must not move).
## ADR
Yes.
## Risks and open questions
- The honesty rules depend on exact wording ("too early to tell", "no clear change"). Translators
need those rules next to the strings.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts`, `_overview/practise-view.ts`
- `packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`

title: Use Intl for dates in the practise card instead of a month list
parent: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-view.ts` formats "on 30 November" with its own
`MONTHS` array and `getUTCDate()`. It works, but it is English only and the first thing a
translation would have to undo.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `nextWords` uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", timeZone:
"UTC" })` (plus `year` when it is not this year), and the `MONTHS` array is gone.
- [ ] The output is identical: the existing tests in `apps/web/test/train/practise.test.ts` pass
unchanged.
- [ ] Add one test for a date in another year.
## Pointers
- Only `practise-view.ts` and its test. About an hour.
- Run `pnpm --filter @ci/web test -- practise` and `pnpm format` before the PR.

title: Message catalogue for the overview and the trainer
parent: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
The overview and the trainer write their words inline: in components, in
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts` and in `_overview/practise-view.ts`. A translator has
no file to work in, and nothing fails when a string is added without a key.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The epic's ADR has picked the library; this issue follows it.
- [ ] Every user-visible string on `/app` and `/app/train` comes from `apps/web/messages/en.json`,
including the plural forms ("1 position", "8 positions").
- [ ] The user's locale comes from their account setting, then the browser, then `en-GB`.
- [ ] A test fails when a key used in code is missing from `en.json`.
- [ ] The English pages are unchanged: the visual baselines do not move.
## Pointers
- `copy.ts` and `practise-view.ts` hold most of the trainer's and overview's words.
- `packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx` already takes a `locale`.
- The parent epic.

title: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader
body: ## Problem
The app is laid out for 390 px and has visual baselines there, but nobody has used it as a phone
app for a week, and at least one thing is broken for screen readers: every animated number
(`Stat`, built on NumberFlow) renders its digits inside a shadow root with no accessible name, so
the overview headline "your accuracy averages 69.2%, with 1.4 blunders a game" reads with blanks
(finding R2-10).
## Who it's for
Players who practise on their phone, and players who use a screen reader.
## Goals
- Every number on every page has an accessible name.
- The trainer and the overview pass a one-week phone diary by a maintainer, with the fixes made.
## Non-goals
- A native app or offline mode.
## Evidence
Most chess.com rapid games are played on phones, so the practice habit lives there too.
## Proposed design
- Fix `Stat` once (sub-issue); every page gets it.
- Add an axe check to the e2e projects for the main pages.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Stat` has an accessible name equal to its formatted value.
- [ ] An axe scan with no serious violations on the overview, trainer, a game review and progress.
- [ ] Touch targets of at least 44 px on the trainer (the existing `touch-targets.spec.ts` check
extended from `/lab/touch-targets` to the real page).
## Test plan
- Unit: `Stat`'s accessible name.
- e2e: axe on the four pages, touch targets on `/app/train`.
## ADR
No, unless the axe rules need exceptions.
## Risks and open questions
- NumberFlow may change its shadow DOM; the test must check the accessible name, not the markup.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`, `apps/web/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts`
- `packages/ui/DESIGN.md` (the accessibility section)

title: Animated numbers are blank to screen readers
parent: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader
body: ## Problem
`Stat` (`packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`) renders the value with NumberFlow, which draws the digits
in a shadow root. The host element has no `aria-label` and no text alternative, so the overview
headline reads "your accuracy averages , with  blunders a game" to text extraction and, very
likely, to screen readers. On screen it looks fine.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The host gets `aria-label` with the formatted value (the same `Intl.NumberFormat` options as
`valueFormat[format]` and the `locale` prop), or a visually hidden span with the formatted
text and the flow marked `aria-hidden`. Pick one and say why in the PR.
- [ ] A test in `packages/ui/test/` that renders `<Stat value={0.692} format="percent" />` and
finds "69.2%" in the accessible name (Testing Library's `getByLabelText` or
`getByText` on the hidden span).
- [ ] No visual change: `pnpm --filter @ci/ui test` passes and the visual baselines do not move.
## Pointers
- Only `stat.tsx` and one test. About 2 hours.
- The `design-system` skill and `packages/ui/DESIGN.md` before the change.

title: Check touch targets on the real trainer page, not only the lab
parent: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader
body: ## Problem
`apps/web/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts` measures touch targets on `/lab/touch-targets` and
`/styleguide`. The trainer, where the player taps a board and three confidence buttons many times a
day on a phone, is not measured.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The spec also visits `/app/train` at 390 px with a seeded session (reuse the setup in
`apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts`) and checks every button and link is at least 44 px in both
dimensions, the same rule the spec already applies.
- [ ] If something fails, fix it with tokens (`pnpm design:check` passes) or list it in the PR.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts`
- CLAUDE.md "UI" has the e2e command. About half a day including the e2e stack setup.

title: Epic: what 1.0 means
body: ## Problem
`docs/SDLC.md` reserves 1.0.0 for the MVP and says it is declared in its own ADR, but nothing
says what the MVP is. Without a list, 1.0 is either never or arbitrary.
## Who it's for
Players deciding whether to rely on Rematch, and contributors deciding what to work on.
## Goals
A written, checkable bar. The proposal:
- a stranger can sign up, link chess.com, and get analysis, a profile, a report and a daily
session without the maintainer's help;
- "Is it working?" has given a verdict to at least one beta player on real data;
- the player can export their data and delete their account;
- a self-hoster can run it from the docs alone on a machine with 8 GB;
- every page passes the accessibility checks of the phone and screen-reader epic.
## Non-goals
- Billing, a hosted service or Lichess by default. Those are decisions after 1.0.
## Evidence
The beta's feedback (ADR 0041) is the input; this list is a starting point for it.
## Proposed design
The ADR lists the bar; each line is a sub-issue or links to an epic. The release that meets it
uses `release-as: 1.0.0` and `"prerelease": false` (see `docs/SDLC.md`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The ADR declaring the MVP bar is merged.
- [ ] Every sub-issue and linked epic is closed.
## Test plan
The full gate on `main` and a fresh self-host from the docs on a clean machine.
## ADR
Yes: the MVP declaration.
## Risks and open questions
- Is a verdict on one beta account enough evidence, or should 1.0 wait for several?
## Pointers
- `docs/SDLC.md` (versioning), ADR 0095, ADR 0041 (private beta)

title: Delete my Rematch account and everything that belongs to it
parent: Epic: what 1.0 means
body: ## Problem
A player cannot delete their Rematch account. `apps/web/src/server/accounts/remove.ts` unlinks
one chess.com or Lichess account, and the "Delete your account?" dialog in
`apps/web/src/app/styleguide/sections/overlays.tsx` is a styleguide demo, not a feature. A privacy
promise without a delete button is not one (ADR 0018).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Delete account" on the account page, behind a confirm dialog that names what goes.
- [ ] Deletes the user and every row that is theirs alone: links, focus, drill items and
attempts, reports, coach chats, sessions. Shared rows stay: `linked_accounts` and its games
can belong to other users too (see the comment on `removeLink`).
- [ ] A Lichess link's stored token is revoked, as `removeLink` does today.
- [ ] A DB test that creates a user with one row in every user-owned table and checks they are all
gone, and that another user linked to the same chess.com account keeps everything.
- [ ] An e2e that deletes an account and cannot sign back in to it.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/accounts/remove.ts`, `db/migrations/` (the foreign keys and cascades)
- ADR 0018 (privacy defaults), ADR 0046 (game read model and access)

title: Export my data as one JSON file
parent: Epic: what 1.0 means
body: ## Problem
A player who leaves, or wants to check what Rematch keeps about them, has no way to take their
data with them.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Download my data" on the account page returns one JSON file: the user, links, focus
history, drill items and attempts, reports and coach chats. Games are listed by platform id,
not copied: they are public on chess.com and may be shared with other users.
- [ ] Only the signed-in user's own rows; a test proves another user's rows never appear.
- [ ] The file has a `version` field and the format is described in `docs/`.
## Pointers
- The table list is the same as the account-deletion sub-issue's; do them together or share the
list.
